intent.name: staff.record.create
intent.summary: Open an employee's record from their accepted appointment letter on the day they join, and fill in the personal details. Two steps, and the agreed terms are carried rather than typed.

request.gloss: just add a new employee directly

routesElsewhere.note: A staff record is created only from an accepted appointment letter, or by migration at go-live. There is no route that types a person straight into employment (BR-1, E1).

request.text: tankhwah bhi likh do
request.gloss: record the salary too

routesElsewhere.note: The agreed salary carries from the letter and is not an ordinary field on this record. It is set separately and seen only by the roles the visibility rule names (BR-2, BR-12).

request.text: classification aur chhutti ka kota set karo
request.gloss: set the classification and leave allowance

routesElsewhere.goesTo: staff.classification.set and staff.leaveallowance.set — UC-12-01-PC-2 and PC-3
routesElsewhere.note: Both block submission (E6, E7) and each is a decision payroll and leave management read.

request.text: purana record system mein daalna hai
request.gloss: we need to load an old record into the system

routesElsewhere.note: Migration at go-live is a bulk load by the School Admin (A1), not a plan.

steps.note: The record opens from the accepted letter. The role, agreed salary and pay basis, start date, notice period and any probation carry across rather than being typed again (BR-2) — retyping is where a figure quietly changes between what was agreed and what is paid.
The personal details the employee gives on the day. The photograph is taken at joining and attached on the screen — a file does not travel in a plan.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where step 2 fails the record exists in Draft carrying the letter's terms, and the details are set again rather than the record opened twice.
plan.atomicity: Not atomic across the two steps. Step 1 creates the record from the letter and step 2 fills in the person's own details. Nothing reaches the staff roster and payroll pays nobody until the record is approved (BR-8, BR-10).

operations.name: staff.record.open
operations.idempotencyKey: letter_id, since one accepted letter produces one record
operations.purpose: Open a staff record from an accepted appointment letter on the joining date.

parameters.name: letter_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No accepted appointment letter matches. A record cannot be created without one (BR-1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the accepted letters with their candidate, role and start date.

parameters.notes: The accepted appointment letter the record is created from (BR-1, E1). Only an approved candidate has one (UC-12-11 BR-12).

parameters.name: joining_date
parameters.notes: The date the person actually attended (BR-1, E2). Not the start date on the letter — somebody who never arrived must not reach the payroll.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The record as opened, with the letter's terms carried.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Carried from the letter, not typed (BR-2).

fields.name: notice_period
fields.description: Carried from the letter. Read at resignation and at termination.

fields.name: contract_end_date
fields.description: Where the contract is fixed-term. Required for one, and the record is flagged as the date approaches (BR-11).

fields.name: salary_visible
fields.description: False to most actors. The agreed salary carries from the letter but is not an ordinary field here (BR-12).

errors.meaning: No accepted appointment letter exists for the person.
errors.note: There is no route that types a person straight into employment (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The candidate has not attended on the joining date.
errors.note: So nobody who never arrived reaches the payroll (BR-1).

errors.meaning: A fixed-term contract carries no end date.
errors.note: A contract that lapsed unnoticed leaves somebody working without one (BR-11).

operations.name: staff.record.details.set
operations.idempotencyKey: staff_id, since a record carries one set of details
operations.purpose: Record the employee's own personal details on the draft record.

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The record opened in step 1.

parameters.name: details
parameters.notes: Name, guardian name, gender, date of birth, identity number, contact number, emergency phone number, email, designation, working hours, salary account and statutory identifiers. Every one is what the employee gave — a planner that filled in a designation from the letter's role has written their post for them. The photograph is attached on the screen.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: fields_missing
fields.description: Required fields still empty. The record cannot be submitted while any remains.

fields.name: photograph_held
fields.description: False until it is attached on the screen. It is used for the ID card.

errors.meaning: The identity number or the email already exists on another record.
errors.note: Two records sharing either is the commonest way a duplicate is created (BR-14). The message names the existing record.

errors.meaning: The emergency number is the employee's own.
errors.note: A number that reaches only the person who has collapsed is not an emergency contact (BR-5).

errors.meaning: A term carried from the letter was supplied here.
errors.note: There is no such field. The terms are carried, not entered (BR-2).

planningRules.rule: Never supply a term that carries from the letter. The role, salary, pay basis, start date, notice period and probation come across untouched (BR-2) — retyping any of them is exactly where the figure paid stops being the figure agreed.
Never open a record without an accepted letter. E1 is BR-1 working: employment starts from a letter somebody accepted, not from a name typed into a form.
Never use the letter's start date as the joining date. The joining date is the day the person actually attended (BR-1, E2), and using the planned one puts somebody who never arrived onto the payroll.
Never invent a personal detail. An emergency number, an identity number or a salary account guessed from anywhere is a fact about a person that nobody gave.
Report the fields still missing. The record cannot be submitted incomplete, and the employee is standing there on their first day.
Never state or repeat the salary. It is not an ordinary field on this record and is visible only to the roles the visibility rule names (BR-12).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A staff record is deactivated and never deleted, because payroll history, ledger entries and audit trails reference it (BR-10, E12). A record opened in error is returned unapproved and left inactive.

parameters.notes: The employment category (BR-3). Leave entitlement and pay both read it, so every value means something to another module — it is never inferred from a designation or a role.

parameters.name: contract_end_date
parameters.notes: Required where the contract is fixed-term (BR-11, E9). The record is flagged as the date approaches, because a contract that lapsed unnoticed leaves somebody working without one.

errors.meaning: The record is approved.

planningRules.rule: Never infer the classification from the designation or the role. A teacher may be permanent, on contract, on probation or part-time, and the four are paid and given leave differently (BR-3).
Never leave a fixed-term contract without an end date, and never invent one. E9 is BR-11 working, and a date a planner chose is when somebody's employment will appear to end.

routesElsewhere.note: The salary is not an ordinary field on this record. It is set separately and governed by its own visibility rule (BR-12).

request.text: record hata do
request.gloss: remove the record

routesElsewhere.note: A staff record is deactivated and never deleted, because payroll history, ledger entries and audit trails reference it (BR-10, E12).

steps.note: One step. A change made by the approving role itself needs no second approval; any other goes to the configured approver (BR-8, A3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A duplicate identity number or email, an emergency number matching the employee's own, and an edit to a carried term all arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the change, its previous value, the reason and who made it together or not at all. Every change is one row with the previous value kept (BR-8). Where the approving role made it, it takes effect at once; otherwise it waits for approval, and the record reads as it did until then.
